title: Illustration / Characters / Eyes / Emotions
slide_intent: Use eye details to communicate state of mind so simple faces can carry distinct emotional readings.
strategic_value: Changes to pupils, eyelids and highlights can help Duolingo’s characters feel playful and relatable without adding complex facial structure.
demonstration: A multirow grid repeats a simple head while varying pupil position and size, eyelids, highlights and other eye marks; the rationale appears at right.
practical_value: Compare how a small eye change alters the apparent expression before changing the whole character.

content_islands.name: Expression grid
content_islands.spec: Arrange repeated peach head shapes in a three-column grid at left, using varied eye constructions to invite comparison.

content_islands.name: Expression methods
content_islands.spec: Place the Emotions heading and paragraph at right, naming pupil size, shiny-eye effects and eyelid changes.

reference_purposes.Intent: The text connects eye changes with personality, state of mind, playfulness and relatability.
reference_purposes.Expression: Repeated heads demonstrate a range of emotional eye treatments.
reference_purposes.Application: The source names pupil scaling, highlights suggesting tears and lowered eyelids as available techniques.

ingredient.name: Expressive eyes
ingredient.role: Make a character’s emotional state visible.
ingredient.application: Vary pupil size, highlights and eyelid position to suit the intended expression.
ingredient.scope: Historical official Duolingo illustration guidance from the 2024–2025 archived snapshot. The examples are available techniques, not a required expression inventory or an emotion-labeling standard.
